current_row.boundary_rationale: Psalm 127's title names Solomon, “A Song of Ascents. By Solomon.” (web:Ps.127.0 = oshb:Ps.127.1, שִׁ֥יר הַֽמַּֽעֲל֗וֹת לִשְׁלֹ֫מֹ֥ה, byte tier), the part's only such ascription (sweep: 12 titles, 1 li-Shlomo). Its opening verse pairs two 'unless Yahweh' clauses about futile labor, “Unless Yahweh builds the house, they who build it labor in vain. Unless Yahweh watches over the city, the watchman guards it in vain.” (web:Ps.127.1), and web:Ps.127.2 extends the same futility to a worker's own daily toil, “It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil, for he gives sleep to his loved ones.” This pair of verses forms a self-contained panel on labor without Yahweh's blessing; web:Ps.127.3 turns to a new subject, children as Yahweh's own gift, without returning to the house-and-city figures, marking the seam between this panel and the psalm's second panel (web:Ps.127.3-web:Ps.127.5).
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating Psalm 127 as one whole-psalm row was considered, since the part's short psalms default to one row, but rejected because the psalm's own two-panel structure — futile labor (web:Ps.127.1-web:Ps.127.2) against Yahweh's gift of children (web:Ps.127.3-web:Ps.127.5) — is a genuine topic change strong enough to carry a division even at five verses.

items.claim: The 127:2|3 seam that divides a 5-verse psalm is warranted by a topic change plus an absence, neither of which is ruled internal-seam evidence in Ps, while the ruled signal that does stand in the bytes is never cited.
items.auditor_grounds: The row divides Psalm 127 (5 WEB / 5 MT verses, identity) at 2|3 against section 6's default of ONE whole_psalm row for a short psalm. Its stated warrant is 'a genuine topic change strong enough to carry a division even at five verses', corroborated only by an absence ('web:Ps.127.3 turns to a new subject ... without returning to the house-and-city figures'). Sections 5 and 6 close the tier-1 internal-seam list to superscriptions, hallelu-Yah/hodu frames, doxologies, acrostic structure and explicit speaker/addressee shifts (with refrain returns, vocative openings and imperative clusters at section 6); a topic change is DISCUSSION texture by section 5, and absence is never counterevidence. Both observed_substrate_signals describe 127:1 alone (the paired 'unless Yahweh' clauses and the doubled watch root, both BYTE-collated at oshb:Ps.127.1) and carry no seam evidence at 2|3 at all. A ruled signal DOES stand in the bytes and is uncited: oshb:Ps.127.2 addresses a 2mp audience with לָכֶ֨ם (WEB 'It is vain for you to rise up early', web:Ps.127.2), and that address is gone at oshb:Ps.127.3, which opens with the presentative הִנֵּ֤ה and third-person description (WEB 'Behold, children are a heritage of Yahweh.', web:Ps.127.3) -- an explicit addressee shift of exactly the ruled class. The seam therefore survives on the bytes, but not on the grounds the row states; recorded as a disagreement with the shipped row's own stated grounds.
items.proposed_change: Field repair only, no respan: re-warrant boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative on the addressee shift (2mp לָכֶ֨ם at oshb:Ps.127.2 dropping to the presentative הִנֵּ֤ה with third-person description at oshb:Ps.127.3), demote the topic change to corroborating texture, and add the shift to observed_substrate_signals, which currently carries no seam signal. items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways under the Ps strategy's own seam law. Ps 127 is a titled identity psalm (crosswalk: 5 WEB / 5 MT verses; the title שִׁ֥יר הַֽמַּֽעֲל֗וֹת לִשְׁלֹ֫מֹ֥ה is the prefix of oshb:Ps.127.1, so web:Ps.127.0 = oshb:Ps.127.1 is the right dual-cite). The row's stated warrant for the 127:2|127:3 cut is a topic change plus an absence ('without returning to the house-and-city figures'); strategy section 5 closes tier-1 internal-seam evidence to superscriptions, hallelu-Yah/hodu frames, doxologies, acrostic structure and explicit speaker/addressee shifts, section 6 adds refrain returns, vocative openings and imperative clusters, and the owner addendum bars absence as evidence - a topic change is discussion texture, so the warrant as stated is not of a ruled class, and both observed_substrate_signals describe oshb:Ps.127.1 alone (the paired אִם יְהוָ֤ה clauses and the doubled watch root יִשְׁמָר / שׁוֹמֵֽר, all byte-collated there) and carry no seam signal at 2|3. The auditor's uncited ruled signal re-derives TRUE: לָכֶ֨ם (oshb:Ps.127.2, word index 1, byte tier) is the psalm's only second-person form (no 2ms/2mp suffix or verb stands in MT 127:1, 3, 4 or 5), and oshb:Ps.127.3 opens on the verse-initial presentative הִנֵּ֤ה (14 such verse-initial verses book-wide, skeleton tier) with third-person description. BOTH SIDES weighed: the preceding unit closes on שָׁ֤וְא לָכֶ֨ם מַשְׁכִּ֪ימֵי ק֡וּם ... כֵּ֤ן יִתֵּ֖ן לִֽידִיד֣וֹ שֵׁנָֽא (oshb:Ps.127.2, byte tier) - 2mp address closing on the sleep clause - and the following unit opens הִנֵּ֤ה נַחֲלַ֣ת יְהוָ֣ה בָּנִ֑ים (oshb:Ps.127.3, byte tier); the explicit addressee shift is the governing rule that decides, corroborated by the presentative onset. Qualification the repair must carry: the 2mp address is confined to MT 127:2 (1 verse), so an addressee criterion alone would mark 1|2 as readily as 2|3; what fixes the seam at 2|3 is that the repetition שָׁ֤וְא binds vv1-2 (3 tokens in 2 verses: oshb:Ps.127.1 word indices 8 and 17, oshb:Ps.127.2 word index 0; word-bound שוא 10 verses book-wide, skeleton tier) and stops there - absent from MT 127:3-5 - while the presentative onset stands at v3. The seam therefore survives on bytes but not on the row's stated grounds: a defective warrant class with the boundary itself sound is medium, not high; the two-row treatment is permissible under section 6 because the panels are divisible at a ruled-class signal, so no span change is proposed and none is warranted. Ruled coherently with the seam-pair partner M8-Ps-431, whose rejected alternative defers to this row's reason and whose first substrate signal already quotes the הִנֵּ֤ה (oshb:Ps.127.3) onset: the matching field repair belongs on both rows as one edit (section 10 seam-pair rule). No selah, no K/Q in Ps 127 (pmarks; paseq count-only, 3 at MT 127:1 and 1 at MT 127:2, inventory-cited, single-witness, no seam role); all three Hebrew runs in the row reproduce byte-for-byte in the staged extract. Repair validated and ENDORSED as a field repair with the qualification above (addressee shift plus the שָׁ֤וְא (oshb:Ps.127.2) tie plus the presentative onset; topic change demoted to texture; the signal added to observed_substrate_signals on both rows). Verdict: confirm at medium; span_ruling n/a.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The unit turns from petition to a notoriously obscure zone: “Let the righteous strike me, it is kindness… Yet my prayer is always against evil deeds” (web:Ps.141.5) marks a speech-act turn from petition to descriptive report, continuing the same 3mp referent web:Ps.141.4 itself names (‘the workers of iniquity’) into third-person description of “Their judges” thrown down “by the sides of the rock” (web:Ps.141.6), and the quoted image “As when one plows and breaks up the earth, our bones are scattered at the mouth of Sheol” (web:Ps.141.7) -- the connective logic across these three verses remains genuinely unsettled in the WEB rendering itself.

items.claim: The row's confidence ground and one of its three observed substrate signals are WEB translation facts (the rendering's unsettled connective logic; WEB quotation marks around 141:7), which are tier-4 and may not corroborate a seam or a confidence band.
items.auditor_grounds: boundary_rationale closes: the connective logic across these three verses remains genuinely unsettled in the WEB rendering itself. observed_substrate_signals[1] is: web:Ps.141.7 is rendered as quoted speech in WEB with no marked speaker. The WEB typography is real (WEB 141:7 is set in double curly quotes and carries a translator footnote) but it is translation punctuation, and MT 141:7 carries no such marking. The MT-side difficulty that would honestly carry the band is present in the bytes and uncited: כִּי ע֥וֹד וּ֝תְפִלָּתִ֗י בְּרָעוֹתֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ps.141.5) and נִשְׁמְט֣וּ בִֽידֵי סֶ֭לַע שֹׁפְטֵיהֶ֑ם (oshb:Ps.141.6). The row's other two substrate signals are byte-supportable (the 3mp chain and the vocative distribution), so the tier-4 items corroborate a seam that does have a text-side warrant.
items.proposed_change: Drop observed_substrate_signals[1] and re-anchor the confidence sentence to MT, e.g. the connective logic across MT 141:5-7 is unsettled in the Hebrew itself (oshb:Ps.141.5, oshb:Ps.141.6).
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. The tier-4 facts are real: web:Ps.141.7 is set in WEB inside curly double quotation marks with a translator footnote, and the row's confidence sentence locates the obscurity 'in the WEB rendering itself'; MT 141:7 carries no such marking. The row splices no Hebrew and cites no oshb: ref, lists the quotation-mark fact as observed_substrate_signals[1] - an evidence slot - and makes the translation-located sentence its only stated ground for its band, so translation punctuation and a translation-located judgement are doing corroboration work (E-23), not standing as stray remarks; that is medium, not low. Not high, because every seam-bearing claim of the row re-derives from MT under ruled classes: the 3mp chain is byte-real - בְּמַנְעַמֵּיהֶֽם (oshb:Ps.141.4, word index 14), בְּרָעוֹתֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ps.141.5, word index 12), שֹׁפְטֵיהֶ֑ם (oshb:Ps.141.6, word index 3), byte tier - and the divine name stands at oshb:Ps.141.1 (יְהוָ֣ה, word index 2), oshb:Ps.141.3 (יְ֭הוָה, word index 1) and oshb:Ps.141.8 (יְהֹוִ֣ה אֲדֹנָ֣י, word indices 2-3) and in no token of MT 141:4-7 (skeleton sweep of the psalm). BOTH SIDES of each seam weighed: at 141:4|141:5 the preceding unit closes on the 2ms jussive petition אַל תַּט (oshb:Ps.141.4, byte tier) running to בְּמַנְעַמֵּיהֶֽם, and this unit opens יֶֽהֶלְמֵֽנִי צַדִּ֨יק חֶ֡סֶד (oshb:Ps.141.5, byte tier) with no second-person form anywhere in MT 141:5-7 (token lists inspected; the second-person forms of MT 141:1-4 include the imperatives ח֣וּשָׁה, הַאֲזִ֥ינָה (oshb:Ps.141.1), שִׁיתָ֣ה, שָׁמְרָ֣ה, נִ֝צְּרָ֗ה (oshb:Ps.141.3), the jussive תַּט (oshb:Ps.141.4) and the suffixed קְ֭רָאתִיךָ, לָֽךְ (oshb:Ps.141.1) and לְפָנֶ֑יךָ (oshb:Ps.141.2)) - the explicit addressee shift is the ruled class that decides, and it is more precise than the row's 'petition to descriptive report', since oshb:Ps.141.5 still carries prefix forms read as wishes (יֶֽהֶלְמֵֽנִי; the negated jussive אַל יָנִ֣י) but drops the addressee; at 141:7|141:8 this unit closes נִפְזְר֥וּ עֲ֝צָמֵ֗ינוּ לְפִ֣י שְׁאֽוֹל (oshb:Ps.141.7, byte tier, first person plural, no address) and the next opens כִּ֤י אֵלֶ֨יךָ יְהֹוִ֣ה אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ps.141.8, byte tier) - a vocative opening and addressee return, ruled in section 6; both rulings cohere with M8-Ps-464 and M8-Ps-466. The medium_low band is well placed (sound edges, obscure interior). Titled identity psalm; no selah, no K/Q in Ps 141 (pmarks; paseq count-only, 1 at MT 141:5, inventory-cited, single-witness, no seam role). Repair validated: dropping observed_substrate_signals[1] is endorsed outright; the proposed MT re-anchoring is ENDORSED with qualification - the runs כִּי ע֥וֹד וּ֝תְפִלָּתִ֗י בְּרָעוֹתֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ps.141.5) and נִשְׁמְט֣וּ בִֽידֵי סֶ֭לַע שֹׁפְטֵיהֶ֑ם (oshb:Ps.141.6) collate at byte tier, but 'unsettled in the Hebrew itself' is an interpretive judgement, not a byte fact, and must be phrased as the row's reading of the clause boundaries and of the subject of נִשְׁמְט֣וּ (oshb:Ps.141.6), while the seam sentence should name the addressee shift rather than a petition-to-report turn. Verdict: confirm at medium; span_ruling n/a.

current_row.boundary_rationale: Psalm 149 opens under the hallelu-Yah frame (opener device, psalm_device_inventory.json verse-initial list) — הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ (oshb:Ps.149.1) — with “Praise Yahweh! Sing to Yahweh a new song, his praise in the assembly of the saints” (web:Ps.149.1), the assembly named בִּקְהַ֥ל חֲסִידִֽים (oshb:Ps.149.1). The unit runs through the causal grounding clause כִּֽי רוֹצֶ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה (oshb:Ps.149.4), “For Yahweh takes pleasure in his people. He crowns the humble with salvation” (web:Ps.149.4), which closes the reason for praise. At web:Ps.149.5 the same prefix-conjugation mood continues on a changed setting — the saints on their beds rather than the dancing assembly of web:Ps.149.3 — and carries the sword theme of web:Ps.149.6, unheralded in 149:1-4; the seam is a discourse turn in setting, not a formal disjunctive marker, since the mood itself runs unbroken from web:Ps.149.2 through web:Ps.149.5.

items.claim: The book-wide saints-term digit (26 verses) counts a consonantal substring, not the two spellings the sentence names; the named object occurs in 10 verses, and the 26 includes a different lexeme.
items.auditor_grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative, observed_substrate_signals[3] and device_notes all read: the saints-term (chasidim/chasidav) recurring at 149:1, 149:5, and 149:9 (3 of 3 Psalm 149 members; 26 verses book-wide, skeleton tier). Re-swept at skeleton tier over the MT verse map: the contiguous consonantal substring chet-samekh-yod-dalet occurs in exactly 26 verses -- that is where the digit comes from -- but the two spellings the sentence NAMES, חֲסִידִ֣ים (oshb:Ps.149.5) and חֲסִידָ֗יו (oshb:Ps.149.9), occur in only 10 verses book-wide (2 and 8 respectively). The 16-verse remainder is other forms (MT 4:4, 12:2, 16:10, 18:26, 32:6, 43:1, 50:5, 52:11, 79:2, 86:2, 89:20, 104:17, 132:9, 132:16, 145:10, 145:17), and MT 104:17's member is חֲ֝סִידָ֗ה -- the stork, a different lexeme -- exactly the contained-substring trap the book's sweep hazard catalog names. The load-bearing half of the sentence, 3 of 3 Psalm 149 members, is byte-TRUE and is what keeps the whole_psalm rival live at medium confidence, so the defective digit is not alone load-bearing. The same sentence is carried on the paired row for 149:5-9 (there as 2 of 3 members; 26 verses book-wide), so any cure is a seam-pair cure installed on both.
items.proposed_change: Either rename the object to match the digit (the saints-root chet-samekh-yod-dalet as a consonantal substring: 26 verses book-wide, skeleton tier, including the homographic stork at MT 104:17) or keep the named spellings and correct the digit to 10 verses book-wide; install the same wording on the paired 149:5-9 row.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes with the staged Ps tools (sweep.py --skel with --tokens, collate.py, verse_map_oshb.json, pmarks_Ps.json); Ps 149 and Ps 104 are identity psalms in web_mt_offset_map.json, so web:Ps.149.N = oshb:Ps.149.N and web:Ps.104.17 = oshb:Ps.104.17, and the row's refs stand in the right space. (1) COUNT OBJECT. The filed digit reproduces ONLY as the contiguous consonantal substring חסיד at skeleton tier: 26 verses / 26 tokens book-wide. It does not reproduce for the object the sentence names. The two named forms, חֲסִידִֽים (oshb:Ps.149.1, byte tier) and חֲסִידִ֣ים (oshb:Ps.149.5, byte tier) for chasidim and חֲסִידָ֗יו (oshb:Ps.149.9, byte tier) for chasidav, sweep at skeleton tier as חסידים = 2 verses (MT 149:1, 149:5) and חסידיו = 8 verses (MT 30:5, 31:24, 37:28, 85:9, 97:10, 116:15, 148:14, 149:9), 10 verses in all, exactly as the auditor filed. The 16-verse remainder (MT 4:4, 12:2, 16:10, 18:26, 32:6, 43:1, 50:5, 52:11, 79:2, 86:2, 89:20, 104:17, 132:9, 132:16, 145:10, 145:17; re-derived list identical to the finding's) is other inflections of the saints-noun in 15 verses plus, at MT 104:17, חֲ֝סִידָ֗ה (oshb:Ps.104.17, byte tier), the stork, “The stork makes its home in the cypress trees.” (web:Ps.104.17), a different lexeme caught by the contained substring, the very class the toolkit's sweep hazard catalog names as the contained-substring trap. So under the most charitable reading (the saints-noun in every inflection) the honest digit is 25 verses; under the reading the wording invites (the two named forms) it is 10; it is 26 under no reading of the words the saints-term, and the label skeleton tier names a collation level, not a licence to count a broader object than the one named (strategy section 10 count-object discipline: every count names WHAT it counts). Tested against the row: this is not a true claim lacking its digit but a digit bound to the wrong object, so the E-05 lane law yields medium, not low. (2) LOAD-BEARING TEST, seam 149:4|5 weighed from both sides. The preceding unit closes at MT 149:4 כִּֽי רוֹצֶ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה … עֲ֝נָוִ֗ים בִּישׁוּעָֽה (oshb:Ps.149.4, byte tier), a causal grounding clause with no ruled closer: Psalm 149 carries no Selah verse (the word-bound Selah inventory is 71 verses book-wide, none in Psalm 149), no refrain, and no K/Q note (pmarks_Ps.json kq: none in Psalm 149, none at MT 104:17), while the hallelu-Yah frame stands only at the psalm's edges, הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ verse-initial at oshb:Ps.149.1 and הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ verse-final at oshb:Ps.149.9 (byte tier). The following unit opens at MT 149:5 יַעְלְז֣וּ חֲסִידִ֣ים … עַל מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָֽם (oshb:Ps.149.5, byte tier), continuing the yod-preformative jussive chain that runs from יִשְׂמַ֣ח (oshb:Ps.149.2, byte tier) through 149:5; the only mood shifts in the psalm fall at 149:1|2 (the imperative שִׁ֣ירוּ of oshb:Ps.149.1 giving way to jussives) and at 149:6|7 (the infinitive-construct chain לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת oshb:Ps.149.7, לֶאְסֹ֣ר oshb:Ps.149.8, לַעֲשׂ֤וֹת oshb:Ps.149.9, all byte tier). The governing rule that decides is therefore that no tier-1 device stands on either side of 149:4|5: the seam is a discourse turn in setting only, which is exactly the posture the shipped row and its paired row M8-Ps-491 (Ps.149.5-Ps.149.9) both hold at medium with the whole_psalm rival live; the seam pair is coherent and this item does not touch it. The row's 3-of-3 recurrence claim is byte-TRUE (חֲסִידִֽים oshb:Ps.149.1; חֲסִידִ֣ים oshb:Ps.149.5; חֲסִידָ֗יו oshb:Ps.149.9; byte tier) and is what keeps the rival live; the book-wide digit only contextualizes it. Correcting the digit to 25 leaves the argument unchanged, and correcting it to 10 would put 3 of the 10 book-wide verses inside Psalm 149 and make the rival MORE live, not less, so the digit cannot flip the seam and is not load-bearing: medium, not high. It is not low either: the same false digit-object pairing is carried three times in the row (strongest_rejected_alternative, observed_substrate_signals[3], device_notes) and mirrored on the paired 149:5-9 row (there as 2 of 3 Psalm 149 members; 26 verses book-wide, where the 2-of-3 is likewise byte-true), so any cure is a seam-pair cure. (3) REPAIR PROPOSAL validated from bytes. Option A (rename the object to match 26 and disclose the stork) is byte-sound only if the object is named as the consonantal string חסיד swept as a contained substring, not as the saints-root: 26 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, of which 25 carry the saints-noun and 1 (MT 104:17) the stork. Option B (keep the two named forms and correct the digit to 10 verses book-wide) is byte-sound as re-swept (2 + 8, with all three Psalm 149 members inside those two forms). A third byte-sound wording is the saints-noun in every inflection, 25 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, excluding the homographic stork at MT 104:17 (token-by-token classification of the 26 hits: 7 singular, 2 plural absolute, 16 suffixed, 1 stork). Each remains a PROPOSAL for owner triage, to be installed identically on M8-Ps-490 and M8-Ps-491; span_change is false, so span_ruling is n/a. Verdict: confirm at medium (E-05 count-object overclaim). Same-model-family corroboration of the auditor's re-sweep, not independent confirmation.
